CGB.CountedPopulation.recovers_from_floo.signature:

        (∀ (y : B) (i : A), 0 < w y i) →
          ∀ (ys : List B) (a : A → ℝ),
            (∀ (i : A), 0 ≤ a i) →

CGB.ConservedMemory.remembers_of_quiet_a.signature:
∀ {U : Type u_1} {Λ : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} {I : Type u_4} {Obs : Type u_5} [inst : Fintype U]
  [inst_1 : DecidableEq U] [inst_2 : Fintype Λ] [inst_3 : DecidableEq Λ] [inst_4 : Fintype A] [DecidableEq Obs]
  [Fintype Obs] (M : CGB.Medium U Λ A I) (W : CGB.World U Λ I),
  M.Clocked W.clock →
    ∀ (observe : (U → Λ) → Obs),
      (∀ (x y : U → Λ), 0 < M.kernel W.clock W.quiet x y → observe y = observe x) →
        ∀ (n₀ : ℕ) (x₀ y : U → Λ) (wquiet wwrite : W.W),
          W.sense wquiet = W.quiet →
            0 < M.law W (fun x => W.sense) n₀ x₀ wquiet →
              0 < M.law W (fun x => W.sense) n₀ x₀ wwrite →
                0 < M.kernel W.clock (W.sense wwrite) x₀ y → observe y ≠ observe x₀ → M.Remembers W

CGB.Medium.p2b_of_conductance.signature:
∀ {U : Type u_1} {Λ : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} {I : Type u_4} [Fintype U] [inst : Fintype A]
  [inst_1 : DecidableEq (U → Λ)] (M : CGB.Medium U Λ A I) (E : (U → Λ) → ℝ) (κ : A → (U → Λ) → ℝ) (rev : A → A),
  Function.Involutive rev →
    (∀ (a : A) (x : U → Λ), M.act a M.calm x ≠ x → M.act (rev a) M.calm (M.act a M.calm x) = x) →
      (∀ (a : A) (x : U → Λ), M.act a M.calm x ≠ x → κ (rev a) (M.act a M.calm x) = κ a x) →
        (∀ (a : A) (x : U → Λ),
            M.act a M.calm x ≠ x → M.rate a M.calm x = κ a x * Real.exp (-(E (M.act a M.calm x) - E x) / 2)) →
          M.P2b

Fixed-energy conductance learning CAN change finite-time predictions.

Three functional commitments do not define a common state transition.

groups.premise: Positive prior precision, nonnegative input weights; softmax criterion includes query/head/bias changes. One-hot equivalence assumes no global decay; mixed keys have an explicit counterexample.

groups.premise: Repeated identical slot evidence, no prior step; probe-family bound needs each absolute deviation within tolerance. Occurrence-decay inequality assumes 0<alpha<=1 and use exponent<=1.

groups.premise: Additive two-source predictor versus a target with nonzero interaction contrast; fixed query for additive-content result.
groups.consequence: Learned cross-history queries or nonlinear interactions must be expressible on the real prediction path. MLP is allowed but not forced; key/query product is an existing witness, not a language model.

groups.premise: Specified joint law for entropy/KL; equally weighted opposite labels for merged-history floor; fixed quadratic and symmetric fresh noise for unbiasedness; deterministic coarsening of a finite nonnegative joint law for CMI.
groups.consequence: Separate missing distinctions from decoder mismatch and current fitting from future value. Reusing existing state for compression is allowed; general language evaluation is not proved unbiased by a quadratic identity.

groups.premise: Gain floor assumes positive process variance and incoming precision floor; variance blowup uses an explicit random-walk error recursion; occurrence-clock comparison is a stationary scalar EMA model.
groups.consequence: Do not freeze all plasticity or force every memory direction to drift. Local gains must remain responsive on drifting directions; Kalman form is one conditional realization.

groups.premise: Pure multiplicative reinvestment has absorbing zero support; coarse/local identities assume a supplied grouping and nonzero group sums; tag contraction uses positive uniform mixing; finite geometric bank covers only its declared delay band.
groups.consequence: Same exchange law can commute with coarse-graining and stay local. Group generation and healthy support recovery still need construction; a bank of clocks is not forced by the horizon bound.

groups.premise: Specific categorical boundary logits and two-term drift; phase-balance necessity assumes proportionality to the score for all logits/targets; outcome-blind zero drift uses sampling from that same policy.
groups.consequence: Observed and predicted contributions may be computed analytically. No separate sleep module follows. Equal live bets stop allocation changes even when all predictors are wrong, so content learning must remain reachable.

groups.premise: Finite physical code versus all real states; stationary loss on a finite body; full-update error recursion and invariant budget must be supplied.
groups.consequence: Charge precision and workspace. Bounded-state indefinite operation is possible without eternal loss descent; a uniform numerical error certificate must not impose global contraction that destroys latches.

groups.premise: Specific finite physical witness for passive intake; actual world access changes recovery for a fixed body. Silence needs action-conditioning only if its law depends on action. Robust-safe action is impossible when every action has a bad allowed outcome.
groups.consequence: Keep system4 boundary open in the design. Predictive compression and intake availability alone do not certify life; use witnesses as semantic controls, not food modules or universal language-body requirements.

groups.consequence: Participation and release can retain history in the same bounded coordinates, without storing a new trace page. A nonzero exact-real product alone does not establish finite-precision decodability.

groups.premise: Nonnegative occupation with total<=1, normalized nonnegative target, bounded inflow/gate/release as stated; endpoint agreement assumes the same state and inputs.
groups.consequence: Release and admission can share one implicit free complement. These are positive-occupation laws, not automatically signed neural-content laws, and total conservation alone does not prevent monopoly.

groups.premise: Zero use exponent for exact no-decay; the actual transition must leave the projection unchanged for the suffix; normalized gain requires positive numerator and positive ordered local demand.
groups.consequence: Do not age untouched content merely because another contact was used. Usage normalization provides one local anti-dominance construction, not a theorem that Adam prevents global winner-take-all or that a use accumulator must be added.

groups.premise: Unequal forward/reverse cycle products; a specific integral-reference fixed point with g(0)=0; two distinct fixed points of a differentiable scalar map, respectively.
groups.consequence: A reference gap vanishes at its adapted fixed point; circulation and a retained alternative are different properties. A slope-one point is necessary in the stated latch family, not sufficient for stable memory. Constrain existing dynamics; no extra clock or reference pool.

groups.premise: The explicit leaveValue threshold family: constant mean and positive learning cost, or two means and cost below one-quarter gap. Improvement is existential at some patch.
groups.consequence: World structure and costs constrain learning benefit. These do not prove the mean is learnable, uniform improvement, or that endless novelty is universally necessary. Use future language evidence, not a new food score.

groups.premise: Both teaching and response vary differentiably with the same parameter. Stopped teaching is complete iff its omitted product vanishes.
groups.consequence: Current autograd can include both terms. Delayed stopped-teaching updates must justify omission; this does not force BPTT, full historical Jacobians, or gradient matching as the only learning objective.

groups.premise: Compatible hidden worlds behind a body state; one action safe for ALL compatible viable worlds (and supported events), plus a viable seed. Exact reachable consequence readout requires merged reachable histories to agree on all action consequences.
groups.consequence: The same historical distinctions support prediction and eventual action. Classical.choice existence is not efficient synthesis or a trained self-model. Universal safety is stronger than probabilistic survival. System 4 remains an interface constraint.
